name: Docket showcase mandate
description: An AI agent whose reputation is computed from what a contract actually let it do. The agent holds a key that can call one function, act(), on a Mandate contract; the mandate refuses anything outside its policy and records the refusal. DCS-1 turns that enforced record into a score anyone can recompute from the mandate's own event log.

skills.name: Bounded native transfer
skills.description: Sends MON to an allowlisted counterparty, within a per-action cap, a rolling window cap, and a rate limit. Every attempt is recorded whether it was allowed or refused.

x-docket.note: deployBlock is load-bearing, not decoration. Monad's public RPC caps eth_getLogs at 100 blocks per request, so a verifier scanning from genesis would need hundreds of thousands of calls. Without a published start block, 'anyone can recompute this' is true in principle and false in practice.

authority.agentCanCall: act(Action) on the mandate, and nothing else
authority.agentCannotCall: approve, increaseAllowance, setApprovalForAll, permit - refused by selector
authority.ownerControls: policy, pause, and the ERC-8004 identity. Tightening is immediate; loosening waits out a timelock.
authority.scorePublishedBy: an independent key that owns nothing and can only post a recomputable claim
